llm_findings: The bounded plan isolates one causal change: BF16 operands at the LM-head projection, followed immediately by FP32 logits. Toggle persistence, logging and offline tests support that change without adding another experimental factor.

Authoritative train.py supports the dtype premise: FP32 per-block lambda tensors promote the residual stream; default norm() preserves its dtype; Linear.forward ignores a BF16 cache for FP32 input and uses the FP32 master weight. GPT.forward applies the head immediately before vocabulary slicing, float conversion and softcap/CE.

Repository evidence supports testing an isolated precision boundary: the BF16-SDPA ledger row records 2233 steps and 1.002028 BPB versus trn22 control's 2076 and 1.005967. This is analogous evidence, not a measurement of LM-head cost; parameter counts alone do not establish its runtime share or prove logits are the largest activation.

The supplied decision log contains no closed LM-head precision direction. This head-only BF16 experiment is materially distinct from the generic full-model FP8 autocast direction closed in CURRENT_STATE.md.

The plan is competition-legal: edits are confined to train.py, training remains from scratch on provided data, evaluator code is untouched, and checkpoint toggle restoration preserves the same head arithmetic for training and standalone evaluation.

The expected effect is falsifiable using the controller-pinned seed-42 full-chip matched comparison: at least 2% more steps and at least 0.001 lower public BPB, with explicit inert, quality-failure and confounded outcomes. Exact disabled-path preservation, layout handling, differentiable master-weight routing and checkpoint restoration remain obligations for the separate implementation review; planned CPU checks are not yet completed evidence or proof of native performance.
